name_note: GTDB names this species Bifidobacterium piotii, while the literature calls it Gardnerella piotii; the genomes GTDB places here are labelled Gardnerella vaginalis, Gardnerella pickettii and Gardnerella piotii in NCBI, so the GTDB species is broader than G. piotii as named in papers.

sentences.text: Gardnerella piotii was described as a new species alongside Gardnerella leopoldii and Gardnerella swidsinskii, in a genome analysis that delineated 13 genomic species within the genus Gardnerella.
In that work, mass spectrometry protein signatures gave peaks differentiating these four species, and only strains of G. vaginalis produced beta-galactosidase.
A study that assessed vaginal species including G. piotii reported that vaginal swabs with high resistant alpha-1,4-glucan degradation activity were associated with bacterial vaginosis.

Combining profiling of a recurrent cystitis cohort with laboratory models, a study reported that G. piotii enhanced uropathogenic Escherichia coli infectivity by producing succinate that upregulated uroplakin via the receptor GPR91.
The same study reported that introducing Lactobacillus crispatus or exposure to lactate partially reduced that E. coli burden in vivo.
